pass_a_gloss: I convicted the erring sect and mastered every passion that is imported rather than native and inevitable. Those native things he accepted of his own will in order to display that the enfleshment is genuine and that native inevitable things are not wicked. Passion therefore drew near the flesh belonging to Gods Word not to gain strength but to be abolished in him; for indecent passions he never entertained even as a fancy. One must now take darkness and world as measured against light that cannot be uttered and cannot be approached. John is an envoy in that he left the wilderness for the settled land so as to announce Christ among the nations. The Lord too is named envoy, not by traveling place to place (deity does not move), but as if stirred from the Fathers embrace and arriving at our want, which is why he is said to lower himself. When the writing uses speech suited to the economy, the phrase he emptied himself marks free royal agency in becoming flesh; the phrase he was sent teaches that the enfleshment was not without the Father. We talk as humans: Father and Son share one counsel even while we distinguish hypostases of one Godhead and substance; thus only the Son took flesh, neither Father nor Spirit. John therefore surpasses the remaining prophets, since they announced one still awaited, whereas he saw him, was convinced by signs that this is the one, and testified from hearing and sight. Saints may be called light, yet not as the Christ confessed in theology, who is light by nature; saints hold illumination by gift. So of Christ it is said: there was the true light. From innate notions the Lord lights rational creatures toward assent that he is God, as they reckon from creaturely beauty and order the superiority of his power. Present in the world as God by care, not by essence. Once more he uproots those who deny that humans and the rest are Gods creatures. World here means humans alone, a part standing for the whole, namely those fixed on worldly things who through earthbound attachment never knew him: idolaters and passion slaves. He came to his own either as enfleshed and visibly recognized, or as coming to those reckoned his by the line from whom is the Christ according to flesh. Cattle offering under the laws figure is no longer required, Christs blood being enough for justification. The Word becoming flesh did not alter essence; made visible by flesh he kept the glory proper to the only begotten Son of God and Father; tent pitcher differs in essence from tent. Avoiding body stops the heavenly body claim; avoiding he became man stops the inner man claim; avoiding flesh arose from the Word stops the change claim. Flesh can be called body, yet not every body is flesh. Hence eat my flesh, and handle me: spirit lacks flesh and bones as you observe in me. Beholding came via magi star, angels, shepherds, Anna, Simeon, Gabriel, the virgins ineffable birth, the Fathers attesting voice, the Spirits resting on him, and myriad signs and cures. As root and fountain of goods he shares without loss; what he gives and creation takes shows Christ is God. For the Adam grace we lost, Christ by…
pass_b_english: —wandering heresy I have refuted, and I have overcome all the passions that are adventitious, not those that are natural and necessary—which he willingly underwent, to show the truth of the incarnation, and that the natural and necessary are not base. For this reason it approached the flesh of the Word of God, not that it might be strengthened, but that in him it might be destroyed; for the shameful passions he did not undergo even in imagination. Darkness and the world are now to be understood by comparison with the inexpressible and unapproachable light.

John is sent as one who has passed from the desert into the inhabited land, that he might proclaim Christ to the peoples. The Lord also was called sent, not as having moved from places to places—for the divine is unmoved—but as somehow moved from the Father’s bosom and having come to our poverty, for which he is also said to have humbled himself. So when Scripture speaks words fitting the economy, if it says that “he emptied himself” (Philippians 2:7), it signifies the self-ruling and royal—that he was incarnate willingly; but if it says that he was sent, it teaches that he was not incarnate apart from the Father. We say these things as human beings; for the will of Father and Son is one, even if we conceive the difference of the hypostases of the one Godhead and essence; thus we say that the Son alone was incarnate, not the Father, not the Spirit.

For this reason John is greater than the other prophets: those proclaimed the one awaited, but this one, having seen him and been persuaded by signs that this is he, came bearing witness from what he heard and saw.

Even if John and the saints are light, they are not so as the Christ who is theologized, who is light by nature; for the saints received illumination by grace. Therefore concerning Christ he says: “He was the true light” (John 1:9).
The Lord enlightens his rational creatures from natural notions unto believing that he is God, as they infer from the beauty and good order of his creatures the excellence of his power.

As God he was in the world not according to essence, but according to providence. Again he pulls up the heresy of those who say that human beings and the rest are not creatures of God. Here he calls “world” only human beings, naming the world from a part—that is, those who mind the things of the world and are nailed to it, who through attachment to earthly things did not know him at all: idolaters and slaves of the passions.

He is said to have come to his own inasmuch as, having been incarnate, he was made known to those who saw him with their eyes, or that he came to his own, who seemed to be his according to “from whom is the Christ according to the flesh” (Romans 9:5).
There is no longer need of cattle-sacrifice as pleasing to God according to the type of the law, since the blood of Christ is sufficient for justification.

When the Word became flesh, he was not changed in essence, but having become visible through the flesh he remained having his own glory as only-begotten Son of God and Father; for the one pitching tent is other in essence from the tent. He did not say “body,” lest some say he wore a heavenly body; nor “he became man,” lest others say he took not the outer but the inner man; nor “from the Word flesh came to be,” lest others say he was changed from this into that. Flesh is also called body, but body is not in every way flesh. Therefore the Lord also said: “he who eats my flesh” (John 6:54), and elsewhere: “Handle me and see, that a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see me having” (Luke 24:39).

How did we behold? Through the star of the magi, the angels, the shepherds, Anna, Simeon, Gabriel, the ineffable birth from the virgin, the Father’s voice bearing witness to him, the Spirit’s descent upon him, and countless divine signs and healings.
